The sons of Levi at the golden calf
22E.6 War is not to be undertaken but by the will of God.

precepts.text: Jeroboam makes two calves of gold and tells Israel these are their gods, driving out true worship and forcing the faithful to seek the Lord in Jerusalem.
precepts.point: Those out of all the tribes who set their hearts to seek the Lord God of Israel come to Jerusalem to sacrifice, and for three years they strengthen the kingdom of Judah and walk in the way of David and Solomon.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 11: Rehoboam Strengthens Judah and the Levites Return

precepts.why:
“Whereupon the king took counsel, and made two calves of gold, and said unto them, It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem: behold thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.” He set one in Beth-el and the other in Dan, “And this thing became a sin.”

That is why the Levites left. Jeroboam “ordained him priests for the high places, and for the devils, and for the calves which he had made”, and cast Levi off from executing the priest's office unto the Lord. So Levi had to return where they could serve: “the Levites left their suburbs and their possession, and came to Judah and Jerusalem.”

The calves drove out true worship and forced the faithful to seek the Lord in Jerusalem. Out of all the tribes, “such as set their hearts to seek the Lord God of Israel came to Jerusalem”, and for three years they strengthened the kingdom of Judah and “walked in the way of David and Solomon.”

precepts.text: The Levites left their suburbs and came to Judah, for Jeroboam cast them off from the priest's office and ordained his own priests for the high places and the devils.
precepts.point: Jeroboam cast out the priests of the Most High, the sons of Aaron and the Levites, and made priests of any man who came to consecrate himself, priests of them that are no gods.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 13: Abijah Stands on the Covenant

precepts.why:
“For the Levites left their suburbs and their possession, and came to Judah and Jerusalem: for Jeroboam and his sons had cast them off from executing the priest’s office unto the Lord.”

That is what Abijah throws at Jeroboam: “Have ye not cast out the priests of the Lord, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites, and have made you priests after the manner of the nations of other lands?” Jeroboam ordained his own priests for the high places and the devils, and made priests of any man who came to consecrate himself “with a young bullock and seven rams”, so that the same might “be a priest of them that are no gods.”

The great multitude trusted in the “golden calves, which Jeroboam made you for gods”, and in priests after the manner of the nations.

precepts.text: For three years they walked in the way of David and Solomon and strengthened the kingdom of Judah.
precepts.point: Asa commands Judah to seek the Most High and to do the law and the commandment. The pattern of Rehoboam warns what happens when a strong king forsakes that law.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 14: Asa Seeks the Most High and Finds Rest

precepts.why:
“So they strengthened the kingdom of Judah, and made Rehoboam the son of Solomon strong, three years: for three years they walked in the way of David and Solomon.”

Walking in the way of David and Solomon is what strengthens the kingdom. Asa walked that way: he “did that which was good and right in the eyes of the Lord his God”, took away the altars of the strange gods, the high places, the images and the groves, and “commanded Judah to seek the Lord God of their fathers, and to do the law and the commandment.” And “the kingdom was quiet before him.”

precepts.text: The Levites left their suburbs and, with a remnant out of all the tribes of Israel who set their hearts to seek the Most High, came to Judah and Jerusalem.
precepts.point: The division began when Rehoboam refused the people and Jeroboam led the ten tribes away, so the southern kingdom (Judah, Benjamin, Levi) and the northern kingdom went their separate ways, and the Levites and a remnant that set their hearts to seek the Most High left the north and came to Judah. This is the same enmity you keep seeing as Jew and Gentile in the New Testament.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
Rehoboam had “Judah and Benjamin on his side. And the priests and the Levites that were in all Israel resorted to him out of all their coasts. For the Levites left their suburbs and their possession, and came to Judah and Jerusalem: for Jeroboam and his sons had cast them off from executing the priest’s office unto the Lord.”

So the southern kingdom was Judah, Benjamin and Levi. And not only the Levites: “after them out of all the tribes of Israel such as set their hearts to seek the Lord God of Israel came to Jerusalem.” A remnant that set their hearts to seek the Most High left the north and came to Judah.

Jeroboam “ordained him priests for the high places, and for the devils, and for the calves which he had made.” The north went one way and Judah another, and that is the line Peter speaks of when he says a Jew may not keep company with one of another nation.

moments.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

points: Remember the Levites were scattered throughout all 12 tribes. The ones that lived with the kingdom of Judah were fine, but the ones that lived with the northern kingdom were not, because when the high holy days would come about, Levi's job was to tell everybody, especially in them three top holidays, we have to go up to Jerusalem to worship. Remember what the woman of Samaria said: you Jews say that in Jerusalem is where men ought to worship.

For Jeroboam and his sons had cast them off from executing the priest's office: they kicked Levi out. We don't want y'all here, cuz y'all trying to get us to do what God says. No, we want to worship idols. And Jeroboam ordained him priests for the high places, and for the devils, and for the calves which he had made.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

points: Look at verse 16: all the northern kingdom was not idolatrous. After them, out of all the tribes of Israel, such as set their hearts to seek the Lord God of Israel came to Jerusalem, like Tobit. A remnant of them did join with the southern kingdom. This is why we read in 2 Chronicles 15:9 where Ephraim, Manasseh, and Simeon, the strangers, some of them went with the kingdom of Judah.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

points: When Rehoboam comes to Jerusalem he gathers a hundred and eighty thousand chosen warriors of Judah and Benjamin to fight against Israel and bring the kingdom back to himself.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 11: Rehoboam Strengthens Judah and the Levites Return

points: The word of the Lord comes to Shemaiah the man of God, telling Rehoboam and all Judah and Benjamin not to go up or fight against their brethren, for this thing is done of the Most High.
They obey the word of the Lord and return from going against Jeroboam, so the war between north and south does not happen.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 11: Rehoboam Strengthens Judah and the Levites Return

points: Rehoboam dwells in Jerusalem and builds cities for defense in Judah, including Bethlehem, Etam, Tekoa, Bethzur, Hebron, and others.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 11: Rehoboam Strengthens Judah and the Levites Return

points: He fortifies the strongholds, sets captains in them, and stores food, oil, and wine behind the walls he has built.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 11: Rehoboam Strengthens Judah and the Levites Return

points: He puts shields and spears in every city and makes them exceeding strong, having Judah and Benjamin on his side.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 11: Rehoboam Strengthens Judah and the Levites Return

points: The priests and Levites out of all Israel resort to Rehoboam, leaving their suburbs and possessions to come to Judah and Jerusalem, because Jeroboam cast them off from the priest's office.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 11: Rehoboam Strengthens Judah and the Levites Return

points: Jeroboam had ordained his own priests for the high places, the devils, and the calves he made, so Levi had to return where they could serve.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 11: Rehoboam Strengthens Judah and the Levites Return

points: Those out of all the tribes who set their hearts to seek the Lord God of Israel come to Jerusalem to sacrifice, and for three years they strengthen the kingdom of Judah and walk in the way of David and Solomon.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 11: Rehoboam Strengthens Judah and the Levites Return

points: Rehoboam takes Mahalath and Abihail as wives who bear him children, then takes Maachah the daughter of Absalom, whom he loves above all his wives and concubines.
He takes eighteen wives and threescore concubines and begets twenty and eight sons and threescore daughters.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 11: Rehoboam Strengthens Judah and the Levites Return

points: He makes Abijah the son of Maachah chief and ruler among his brethren, intending to make him king, and he deals wisely by dispersing his children through the countries of Judah and Benjamin with abundant provision.
